results.evidence: New evidence cuts the other way from the first pass. The WTA hike entry for Primus Peak (19.0 mi round trip, 7,300 ft) says the peak is most often reached from the Thunder Creek Trailhead at Colonial Creek. A 2024 Inspiration Traverse report started at the Eldorado trailhead but exited over Primus down the Borealis Glacier and the Lucky Pass boot trail to Thunder Creek, and a 2015 report reached Primus's south face from the Eldorado side across the ice cap. Both approaches are genuinely used. The row's prose (approach, itinerary) describes Eldorado, while its pins and approach_logistics describe Thunder Creek. Reconciling them needs a decision on which approach this row describes, plus pin work, so no patch.

results.fact: One-way distance: approach says 18-20 miles one way; itinerary totals about 20 miles round trip
results.evidence: The only published total found is 19.0 mi round trip with 7,300 ft of gain, which is roughly the approach text's '18-20 miles' figure. So that figure is most likely a round-trip number mislabelled as one way, and it agrees with the itinerary's ~20 mi round trip. But that total is tied to the Thunder Creek approach, not the Eldorado approach the approach text describes, and no source gives an Eldorado-side one-way distance to Primus. Since the trailhead question is itself open, the sentence is not rewritten.

No new source gives different per-pitch lengths. The route database publishes both the 450 ft total and the ~120/200/100/170 ft pitches that pitch_detail mirrors, so the gap comes from the published beta itself: the rope-out along a left-trending, wandering line is longer than the face height. Neither figure can be shown wrong.

A regional outdoors write-up describes the 600 ft south face with a 7-pitch breakdown (pitch 4 5.8 70 ft, pitch 5 5.8 50 ft through the chockstone tunnel, pitch 6 5.9 70 ft, pitch 7 5.9+ 140 ft, with 1-2 and 3-4 linkable into ~180 ft pitches). That is a different pitch division from the row's 6 pitches and from other sources, so it cannot be used to correct pitch_detail's lengths. length_m (600 ft) stays within the published 500-650 ft range.

No second source exists for this little-travelled 2015 line. The only account gives 5 pitches and 450 ft, which agrees with length_m and rope_note but gives no per-pitch lengths, so pitch_detail's lengths (sum ~541 ft) cannot be corrected by research.

results.fact: number of sections/pitches on the route
results.evidence: The route database page's description is the first-ascent write-up. It now reads '10 pitches' and lists P1-P10, the last two ('The Ladder'/'The Keyhole', then to the summit) added a year later to reach the true summit, while its header metadata still says 8 pitches, 670 ft. The row's overview ('ten-section') and beta (which describes all ten) match the 10-pitch write-up, and pitches=8 matches the header. But both come from one author's single write-up (the other copy is the same party's summit write-up), so there are not two independent sources to set pitches to 10.

The additional sources checked (a regional outdoors write-up with its own skill/fitness scale, a climbing-magazine route page, and a 2002 trip report) confirm the 5.7 crux but none states a commitment numeral. The Grade II vs Grade III split among the sources already tried stands, so grade, commitment and alpine_grade are unchanged.

results.fact: Waypoint list names 'Red Pass' as a mid-route junction, but the route's own prose never goes there
results.correct_value: The scramble leaves the Commonwealth Creek trail at a cairn before the small pond; Red Pass lies further along the same trail and is not on this route's line. The 'Red Pass' pin should be dropped or replaced by a pin at the cairn turnoff.
results.evidence: The contradiction is confirmed and the sources already tried settle the geography. The fix, though, is removing or relocating a pin (the 'Red Pass' waypoint carries only a name, a type and coordinates, with no note or elevation to correct), and pins are outside this pass. Renaming it would put a wrong label on the Red Pass coordinate. Left for pin work.

results.fact: Which drainage/trail the approach to Rimrock Ridge uses
results.evidence: A fresh search found no ascent account of Rimrock Ridge. The nearby Agnes Creek/Gunsight reports cover other peaks and do not describe a line to this ridge. With no source naming an approach, rewriting the approach text would be invention, so it still needs a human with a map.

results.fact: Slope aspect of the switchbacks: 'southeast-facing' (itinerary note, sectionBreakdown note) vs 'south/southwest-facing' (approach, face, descent_text)
results.evidence: The terrain was sampled with USGS 1 m ground heights (N/S/E/W differences ~130 m apart) along the straight line between the row's trailhead-area and artillery-sign pins. The lower slope (47.780-47.784 N) faces due south (~180 degrees), and the upper slope (47.7875-47.790 N) faces east-southeast (~100-110 degrees). Neither 'southwest' nor a single 'southeast' fits the whole climb, and the real trail line is not known from the pins. This is one topo source with no second source, so nothing is patched.
